title: Placer deux pronoms ensemble
summary: Combine direct, indirect, reflexive, y and en pronouns before the verb they belong to.
objectives: Order pronouns from their grammatical role.
Place a pronoun group before a simple verb, auxiliary or relevant infinitive.
Retain quantities and appropriate participle agreement.

sections.title: Use the order slots, not English word order
paragraphs: A direct object answers whom/what without a preposition in the French construction. An indirect object depends on a preposition, often à. Pronouns replace these complements: le/la/les for direct objects; lui/leur for many à-person objects; me/te/nous/vous can be direct or indirect depending on the verb.

Before a verb, the ordering slots are: me/te/se/nous/vous → le/la/les → lui/leur → y → en. These are ordering options, not an instruction to fill every slot or combine incompatible complements. With first/second-person indirect objects, put me/te/nous/vous before le/la/les; with third-person indirect objects, put le/la/les before lui/leur.

Lui can mean to him or to her; leur means to them and never adds s as a pronoun. Me, te, se, le and la elide before a vowel: m', t', s', l'. Indirect pronouns are selected by the actual French verb, not by an English translation.

examples.french: Je donne le plan à Nora. Je **le lui** donne.
examples.english: I give the map to Nora. I give it to her.
examples.note: Direct le precedes third-person indirect lui.

examples.french: Tu prêtes les outils à ton voisin. Tu **les lui** prêtes.
examples.english: You lend the tools to your neighbour. You lend them to him.
examples.note: The direct object's number does not change lui.

examples.french: Elle explique la règle à nous deux. Elle **nous l'**explique.
examples.english: She explains the rule to the two of us. She explains it to us.
examples.note: First-person indirect nous comes before direct l'.

examples.french: Ces photos ? Je **les leur ai envoyées**.
examples.english: Those photos? I sent them to them.
examples.note: The group precedes the auxiliary; envoyées agrees with preceding photos.

mistakes.why: Direct le precedes third-person indirect lui.

sections.title: Reflexive pronouns occupy the first slot
paragraphs: A reflexive pronoun points back to the subject: me, te, se, nous, vous, se. It comes before a direct-object pronoun. In se laver les mains, se means to/for oneself and les mains is direct; replacing les mains by les yields se les laver.

In compound tenses, both pronouns precede the auxiliary. A preceding direct les can trigger participle agreement even when se is indirect. Compare elles se sont lavé les mains and elles se les sont lavées.

examples.french: Je **me les** rappelle très bien, ces vacances.
examples.english: I remember those holidays very well.
examples.note: Se rappeler quelque chose has a direct object.

examples.french: Les mains ? Elles **se les sont lavées** avant le repas.
examples.english: Their hands? They washed them before the meal.
examples.note: Les is now a preceding feminine plural direct object.

sections.title: En follows indirect pronouns; y follows direct pronouns
paragraphs: En replaces a de-complement or an indefinite/partitive quantity. Keep an expressed number or quantity: je lui en donne trois. An indirect person pronoun comes before en: m'en, t'en, lui en, nous en, vous en, leur en.

Y replaces a location or some à-thing complements. A direct pronoun precedes y: je l'y mets. Do not use y as a general replacement for à + person; verbs may require lui/leur or a stressed form such as à elle. If both y and en are justified, y precedes en: il y en a trois. Do not manufacture two pronouns when only one complement exists.

examples.french: J'offre des places aux bénévoles. Je **leur en** offre quatre.
examples.english: I offer places to the volunteers. I offer them four.
examples.note: Recipient leur, quantity en, retained number.

examples.english: She told me about it yesterday.
examples.note: Me = to me; en = about it.

examples.french: Je mets la boîte dans le coffre. Je **l'y** mets.
examples.english: I put the box in the boot. I put it there.
examples.note: Direct l' comes before location y.

examples.french: Des chaises dans la réserve ? Il **y en** a six.
examples.english: Chairs in the storeroom? There are six there.
examples.note: Y precedes en; the number remains.

mistakes.why: The indirect person pronoun precedes en.

sections.title: Rester clair sans tout remplacer
paragraphs: The order rule tells you where pronouns go, not what the listener can identify. An antecedent is the earlier noun or expression a pronoun refers to. If two plausible antecedents share the same gender and number, repeating one noun is often clearer than using a technically correct two-pronoun group. You do not earn clarity by replacing the maximum number of words.

Me, te, nous and vous can also be direct objects before y: someone meets, takes or accompanies a person somewhere. Find the verb's construction first. Accompagner quelqu'un is direct, so m'y can mean me there, not only to me about it. Elide me/te before y, keep nous/vous intact, and place the group before the verb it completes.
points: A noun can remain explicit while another complement becomes a pronoun. Lui and leur do not identify a recipient's gender.

examples.french: Le badge et le carnet sont prêts pour Adam. Je **donne le badge à Adam** et je garde le carnet.
examples.english: The badge and notebook are ready for Adam. I give the badge to Adam and keep the notebook.
examples.note: Le lui alone would not say which masculine object is being given.

examples.french: Les documents sont pour la comptable, pas pour la directrice. Je **les envoie à la comptable**.
examples.english: The documents are for the accountant, not the director. I send them to the accountant.
examples.note: Keep the recipient explicit while replacing the documents.

examples.french: Tu connais ce laboratoire ? La responsable **m'y attend**.
examples.english: Do you know that laboratory? The manager is waiting for me there.
examples.note: Me is a direct object, y is a location.

examples.french: Le rendez-vous est au conservatoire. Un collègue va **nous y conduire**.
examples.english: The appointment is at the conservatory. A colleague is going to drive us there.
examples.note: Nous y belongs before conduire, not before va.

sections.title: Attach the group to the verb it completes
paragraphs: With a simple tense, pronouns stand before that verb. With a compound tense, they stand before the auxiliary. With an ordinary modal plus infinitive, they stand before the infinitive they complete: je vais le lui expliquer. Do not move them before vais if their roles belong to expliquer.

In a negative finite clause, ne precedes the pronoun group and pas follows the conjugated verb or auxiliary. Negative commands keep this pre-verbal pattern; affirmative commands have a different order taught next.

examples.english: I am going to explain it to them tomorrow.

examples.french: Nous **ne les lui avons pas prêtés**.
examples.english: We did not lend them to him/her.
examples.note: Les refers to masculine plural objects; negation surrounds the auxiliary group.

practice.prompt: Replace only à l'atelier by y, keeping m': Tu m'accompagnes à l'atelier. Supply the two-pronoun group before accompagnes.
practice.explanation: Me is the direct object of accompagner and comes before location y; it elides.

practice.prompt: Both the contract and the timetable are masculine singular and under discussion. Which handover names unambiguously what Lina receives?
choices: Je donne le contrat à Lina.
answers: Je donne le contrat à Lina.
practice.explanation: Correct pronoun order cannot choose between two competing antecedents.

practice.prompt: Replace only dans le hall by y: La guide nous attend dans le hall. Supply the two pronouns before attend.
practice.explanation: Nous is direct here: attendre quelqu'un. It precedes the place pronoun.

practice.prompt: Avoid ambiguity between two recipients. Replace only les devis, retaining à Malik: Je présente les devis à Malik. Supply the full sentence.
practice.explanation: Replacing the direct object does not oblige you to replace the recipient as well.

practice.prompt: Replace au dépôt by y while retaining te: Je peux te conduire au dépôt. Supply only the pronouns plus conduire after peux.
practice.explanation: Te is the direct object of conduire, elides before y, and belongs with the infinitive.

practice.prompt: Two women have just been mentioned. Does lui in Je lui en ai parlé identify which woman without more context?
choices: No; a name or clearer context may be needed.
Yes; lui can refer only to a man.
answers: No; a name or clearer context may be needed.
practice.explanation: Lui can mean to her or to him; grammar alone does not resolve an ambiguous reference.

practice.prompt: Replace le dossier and à ma collègue with pronouns. Supply only the group: Je ___ donne.
practice.explanation: Direct le before indirect lui.

practice.prompt: Replace les mains with les: Elle se lave les mains. Supply only the two pronouns before lave.
practice.explanation: Reflexive se occupies the first slot.

practice.prompt: Replace des conseils and à ses enfants: Elle donne des conseils à ses enfants. Supply only the pronouns before donne.
practice.explanation: Indirect recipient before en.

practice.prompt: Replace les sacs and dans le couloir: Je mets les sacs dans le couloir. Supply only the pronouns before mets.
practice.explanation: Direct les before location y.

practice.prompt: Replace la réponse by la, keeping me: Tu me donnes la réponse. Supply only the two pronouns before donnes.
practice.explanation: Me precedes a direct third-person pronoun.

practice.prompt: Replace les clés and aux voisins with pronouns. Supply only the group: Nous ___ rendons.
practice.explanation: Direct les before third-person indirect leur.

practice.prompt: Complete the pronoun group replacing les pieds: Nous nous lavons les pieds. Nous ___ lavons.
practice.explanation: The subject is already supplied; reflexive nous remains.

practice.prompt: Replace trois billets with en plus retained number: Je donne trois billets à Léa. Fill only the pronoun group: Je ___ donne trois.
practice.explanation: Lui replaces à Léa; en replaces billets while three remains.

practice.prompt: Replace le colis and au bureau: Elle apporte le colis au bureau. Supply only the pronoun group before apporte.
practice.explanation: Le elides before y.

practice.prompt: Replace le règlement and aux élèves. Complete only the missing infinitive group: Je vais ___. Use expliquer.
practice.explanation: Pronouns belong before the infinitive expliquer.

practice.prompt: Supply only envoyer's participle: Ces cartes, je les lui ai ___.
practice.explanation: Les refers to preceding feminine plural cartes.

practice.prompt: Choose the standard negative sentence.
choices: Je ne le lui ai pas dit.
Je le ne lui ai pas dit.
answers: Je ne le lui ai pas dit.
practice.explanation: Ne precedes the whole pronoun group.

practice.prompt: Replace de cette affaire while retaining nous: Elle nous parle de cette affaire. Supply only the pronouns before parle.
practice.explanation: Nous precedes en.

practice.prompt: Supply laver's participle: Les mains, elles se les sont ___.
practice.explanation: Preceding les is the feminine plural direct object.

practice.prompt: Put y and en in order: Des livres ici ? Il ___ a beaucoup.
practice.explanation: Y precedes en.

practice.prompt: Replace les horaires but retain vous: Je vous envoie les horaires. Supply only the two pronouns before envoie.
practice.explanation: First/second-person pronouns precede le/la/les.

production_task.prompt: Write a handover note about keys, a storage place and tickets for volunteers. Introduce each referent before replacing it with a two-pronoun group.
production_task.model_answer: Les clés sont pour la responsable : je les lui donnerai demain. Les boîtes vont dans la réserve : je les y déposerai ce soir. Les bénévoles demandent des billets ; nous leur en réserverons dix.
production_task.translation: The keys are for the manager: I will give them to her tomorrow. The boxes go in the storeroom: I will put them there this evening. The volunteers are asking for tickets; we will reserve ten for them.
rubric: Every pronoun has a clear referent.
Direct/indirect, direct/y and indirect/en orders are correct.
The quantity with en remains expressed.
The note is understandable without reconstructing missing context.
